verdict_reason: The alpha=1 MST/slope estimator is bit-exact with GPTID, but the paper's general law E_alpha(n) proportional to n^(1-alpha/d) inverts to d=alpha/(1-m), while BLME always returns 1/(1-m). On a seeded 3-D cloud alpha=0.5 produced 8.269645 instead of the formula-correct 4.134823, exactly 2x; the released code shares this defect, so reference-code parity does not rescue paper fidelity.
comparable_reason: PHD is intended as intrinsic rather than ambient dimension, and the 66-model sweep found no significant association with d_model (rho=+0.196, p=0.114), n_layers (+0.210, p=0.090), vocabulary (-0.084, p=0.504), or parameter count (+0.133, p=0.286). YELLOW remains because models tokenize the same documents into different pooled point populations and the fixed 2,000-point union cap does not preserve the source's per-text estimand.
github_reason: Fetched official commit 8c8759ef94c8769e2f40f3e507f270e4c948a562 and ran its IntrinsicDim.PHD/prim_tree on identical seeded clouds; the current focused suite exercises the real module and all seven PHD parity tests passed, with recorded alpha=1 fit_transform differences exactly 0. The released code shares BLME's 1/(1-m) inversion and therefore matches even where both depart from the paper for alpha!=1; reference parity does not cure paper infidelity.
paper_reason: Tulchinskii et al. Table 1 reports Wikipedia PHD 9.491+/-1.010. The retained local reproduction using BLME's unchanged estimator under the paper's RoBERTa-base, per-text, special-token-stripped protocol gave 9.233+/-1.120 (2.72% relative mean error), while official GPTID on the same clouds gave 9.238+/-1.187; the public pooled task does not reproduce this protocol.
confounds_reason: Across 66 models every tested size correlation was nonsignificant (largest |rho|=0.210, smallest p=0.090). The pooled/tokenizer protocol is a comparability caveat and changes the estimand, but current evidence does not support calling the reported value a dominant width, depth, vocabulary, or parameter proxy.
defects: CODE phd_dimension.py:176-180 omits alpha from the inversion: the correct paper formula is d=alpha/(1-m); the current config-reachable alpha=0.5 path returns exactly 2x the correct result.

CODE phd_dimension.py:183-250 concatenates token embeddings from all texts and evaluate fits one PHD, while the source computes one manifold and one PHD per text before aggregating; pooled values were 22%-53% above per-text means across prior allowed-model checks.

CONFIG defaults.yaml:332-344 uses a fixed pooled schedule range(50,512,40), n_points=7 and a 2,000-point cap rather than the paper's per-text adaptive schedule; this is separate from the structural pooling CODE defect.
CONFIG omits max_length, so the uncached code fallback uses 128 while the shared cache uses its own longer truncation, constructing different clouds for the same nominal task.
The stochastic task emits neither per-document dispersion nor full-pipeline repeated-seed uncertainty, despite the paper reporting a distribution and the cap draw contributing measurable variation.
fix: Return alpha/(1-m), or reject alpha!=1 and remove it from public configuration. Implement one special-token-cleaned cloud and adaptive schedule per document with mean and uncertainty across texts; otherwise rename the existing output pooled_corpus_phd. Pin max_length identically across cache routes and report repeated-seed uncertainty including the cap draw.
